question: I've been hiking on snow all day and now my eyes burn and everything looks hazy. What is this?
keyPoints: This is snow blindness, caused by UV exposure reflected off snow
Prevention is eye protection: sunglasses or goggles with full UV protection, helped by a wide-brimmed hat or visor
Get the eyes out of the light and covered, and seek care if it does not settle
redFlags: Advises rubbing or rinsing the eyes with snow
Says the condition is permanent blindness

cite.quote: Prevention is crucial in avoiding snow blindness. To protect the eyes from excessive UV radiation, wear sunglasses or goggles that provide 100 percent UV protection

question: My friend hit his head on a rock and seems confused. How do I know if it's serious?
keyPoints: A concussion is a brain injury from a blow or jolt that moves the brain inside the skull
Seek medical attention when signs are present, because severity ranges from mild concussion to serious brain trauma
Symptoms can appear right away or develop gradually, so keep watching him
redFlags: Says it is safe to ignore symptoms if he seems fine at first
Advises keeping the person awake all night as the treatment

cite.quote: The above symptoms can occur immediately after the injury or may develop gradually over time.

question: How long do I hold pressure on a hemostatic dressing?
keyPoints: Hold direct, firm pressure for at least three minutes
Hemostatic dressings are for bleeding where a tourniquet cannot be applied, such as the groin, armpit or neck
redFlags: Gives a hold time materially shorter than three minutes
Says to pack a hemostatic dressing into the abdomen or chest

cite.quote: These dressings should be applied with direct and firm pressure and held for at least three minutes.

question: Can I pack a wound in someone's belly to stop the bleeding?
keyPoints: No — do not pack hemostatic dressings into the abdomen or chest
Wound packing is for sites like the groin, armpit or neck where a tourniquet will not work
redFlags: Says it is acceptable to pack the abdomen or chest
Recommends pushing protruding organs back inside

cite.quote: Do not pack hemostatic dressings into the abdomen or chest.

question: A scalp cut is bleeding way more than it looks like it should. Is that normal?
keyPoints: Yes — the face and scalp are richly supplied with blood vessels, so these wounds bleed heavily
Control it with direct pressure
An avulsion, where a blow separates the scalp from the skull, is a more serious form of this injury
redFlags: Treats heavy scalp bleeding as proof of a skull fracture
Advises applying a tourniquet to the head or neck

cite.quote: The face and scalp are richly supplied with blood vessel

question: How can I tell if an unconscious person's airway is open?
keyPoints: If the casualty is awake and talking, the airway is open
An unconscious casualty cannot demonstrate this, so the airway must be opened and checked
An open airway still does not guarantee they are breathing adequately
redFlags: Advises putting fingers blindly into the throat to sweep for an obstruction
Says an unconscious person always has a clear airway

cite.quote: If the casualty is awake and talking, you can assume the casualty's airway is open.

question: How deep should chest compressions be on an adult?
keyPoints: At least two inches, about five centimetres, for an adult
Heel of the hand on the centre of the chest, between the nipples
The person must be on a firm, flat surface
redFlags: Gives an adult compression depth well under two inches
Gives the adult hand technique for an infant instead of two or three fingers

cite.quote: For adults, compress the chest at least two inches (five centimeters) deep.

question: Do I use both hands to do CPR on a baby?
keyPoints: No — for infants or children use two or three fingers rather than the whole hand
Compressions still go on the centre of the chest with the person on a firm, flat surface
redFlags: Advises using the heel of the hand or both hands on an infant

cite.quote: For infants or children, use two or three fingers instead of the entire hand.

question: Why do people make such a fuss about ticks?
keyPoints: Ticks can carry and transmit disease
Insects and related pests cause irritation and can trigger severe allergic reactions in some people
redFlags: Advises burning a tick off or smothering it with petroleum jelly
Says ticks are harmless

cite.quote: Ticks. Ticks can carry and transmit diseases,

question: Someone is unresponsive but I think they fell. Should I tilt their head back to open the airway?
keyPoints: Head-tilt and chin-lift is for patients with NO history of trauma
A fall is trauma, so this manoeuvre is not the right choice here
Lay the person face up on a flat, firm surface and protect the airway without moving the neck
redFlags: Recommends head-tilt chin-lift for a trauma patient without qualification

cite.quote: To be used for patients with altered mental status who may not be able to protect the airway, with NO history of trauma

question: Someone got stung and now has a rash, swollen mouth and is wheezing. What's happening?
keyPoints: This pattern indicates a severe allergic reaction
Difficulty breathing with stridor or wheezing, skin rash and swelling of the mouth is the recognised combination
It is a medical emergency needing urgent care
redFlags: Treats it as an ordinary local sting reaction
Advises waiting to see whether it worsens before acting

cite.quote: Difficulty breathing, stridor/wheezing, skin rash, swelling of mouth Severe allergic reaction

question: My friend fell a long way and has bad pain around his hips. What should I be worried about?
keyPoints: Pelvic fractures can cause life-threatening bleeding by damaging blood vessels next to the fracture
The pelvis is a ring, so a binder brings the displaced bones together and helps limit internal bleeding
Treat pain in and around the pelvis after injury as a reason to immobilise and get help
redFlags: Advises repeatedly springing or rocking the pelvis to test for a fracture
Treats hip pain after a long fall as a minor bruise

cite.quote: Pelvic fractures can cause life-threatening haemorrhage by damaging blood vessels adjacent to the fractures.
